title: Zero-input isolated rigid body does not invent motion
claim: For the exact L0.0 isolated-body configuration, the measured position, velocity, kinetic energy, contact count, and externally applied work remain within the preregistered stationary-body gates for 60 Jolt integration intervals.
scope: One unjointed 2 kg RigidBody3D at 60 physics ticks per second, gravity_scale 0, zero initial velocity, zero linear and angular damping, no contacts, no controller, no application receipts, no interventions, and the full_contacts_v1 observer with a 32-contact cap.
mechanism: With measured gravity equal to zero and sealed command, application, intervention, and contact streams proving that no external operation was applied, linear momentum should remain zero. This experiment tests whether the engine fixture and observer preserve that zero-input baseline; it does not test support or actuation.
applicability: Calibrating the BR1 flight recorder before articulated experiments
Detecting invented translation, velocity, energy, or contacts in an isolated unary rigid-body fixture
failure_boundaries: Does not establish standing, bracing, fall arrest, getting up, gait, or walking
Does not exercise joints, motors, tendons, muscles, contact reactions, friction, or support geometry
Does not generalize from one rigid body to articulated or soft-body morphologies
Does not establish the effect of changing gravity, damping, mass, timestep, or observer profile because those require separate sweeps or paired controls
unknowns: Whether the same analytic agreement holds across the preregistered L0.1 timestep sweep under gravity
Whether nonzero initial momentum is preserved in the L0.2 ballistic control
Whether full contact instrumentation stays inside the L0.3 observer parity envelope
Whether BR2 can certify articulated inertia and angular momentum without unavailable channels
